name: traceroost-dashboard
description: Agentic AI monitoring and observability — OTEL traces and local log file ingestion for Copilot, Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode. VS Code extension, npx, and Docker.

walkthroughs.title: Get Started with TraceRoost
walkthroughs.description: Observe and debug your AI agent sessions in real time.

steps.title: What is TraceRoost?
steps.description:
TraceRoost gives you a live observability dashboard for GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, and Codex — token usage, latency, file changes, and loop detection.

[Open TraceRoost Sidebar](command:workbench.view.extension.traceroost)

steps.title: Agents Are Ready
steps.description: TraceRoost automatically configured your agents to send telemetry to the local collector. Restart any running sessions to start collecting traces. Past session history is already loading from local log files — no restart needed to see it.

steps.title: Start an Agent Session
steps.description: Run Copilot, Claude Code, or Codex and the dashboard will populate in real time.

steps.title: Open the Full Dashboard
steps.description:
The sidebar shows a live summary. Open the full dashboard in an editor panel for traces, diffs, alerts, cost estimation, export, and more.

[Open Dashboard](command:traceRoost.openDashboard)

steps.title: Detect Loops and Inefficiencies
steps.description: The Sessions tab surfaces five failure patterns per session — deadlocks, error spirals, context accumulation, and more. The Advisor tab analyzes patterns across sessions to generate specific suggestions for improving your agent instruction file.

traceRoost.otlpPort.description: Local port for OTLP trace receiver

traceRoost.autoConfigureAgents.description: Automatically write OTEL telemetry settings into Claude Code's (~/.claude/settings.json), Codex's (~/.codex/config.toml), and GitHub Copilot's own configuration so they send session data to TraceRoost. Runs on every activation but only rewrites a file when something's actually missing, so it's silent after the first successful run (shows a notification only when it changes something). Disabling this leaves your agents' configuration untouched — you can still trigger it manually with the Configure OTEL button in Settings, configure OTEL by hand (see the Help tab), or rely on traceRoost.enableLogIngestion alone. Codex and Copilot CLI sessions have little to show without OTEL: their log files carry only aggregate totals, no per-turn tool calls or responses.

traceRoost.enableOtelIngestion.description: Accept incoming OTEL span data. The OTLP server keeps listening on traceRoost.otlpPort regardless; disabling this silently drops received payloads without storing them.

traceRoost.enableLogIngestion.description: Read local session logs for Claude Code, Codex, and Copilot CLI as a data source. Log data has lower fidelity than OTEL — timing, speed, and loop signals are not available for Codex and Copilot CLI, whose log files carry only aggregate totals. Log and OTEL sessions are shown as separate entries rather than merged. Loading is done incrementally in the background and will not block the UI.

traceRoost.enableMcpServer.description: Start the TraceRoost MCP server so Claude Code can query your session history. The server listens on traceRoost.mcpPort (default 4316). See the TraceRoost Help tab → Agent Integration for setup instructions.

traceRoost.mcpPort.description: Local port for the TraceRoost MCP server (when traceRoost.enableMcpServer is true). Configure Claude Code to connect with: { "mcpServers": { "traceroost": { "url": "http://localhost:4316/mcp" } } }

traceRoost.sessionRetentionDays.description: How many days to keep session history in the local database. Older sessions (and their blob files) are deleted automatically on activation and every 24 hours.
